Your website gets visitors. So why is nobody enquiring?

Most of the time it's not the design. It's the first screen.

A clinic in Velachery doesn't need a fancy slider. It needs:
→ what you do, in one line
→ where you are
→ one clear button: Book an appointment

If a visitor has to scroll just to figure out what to do next, they leave.

Want a website that actually brings enquiries? Book a free consultation (link in the reply).

post.linkedin_text:
One shoot day can give you a month of reels. But only if you plan it before the camera comes out.

I think this is where a lot of businesses lose time. They book a shoot, show up, and then decide what to film. So half the day goes in just figuring things out.

Here's how I'd plan it this week:

1. Write down 8 ideas before the day. Not full scripts, just one line each. For a cafe: "how we make our filter coffee" or "3 things to order on your first visit".

2. Group them by location. All the kitchen shots together, all the counter shots together. Moving the setup again and again eats the day.

3. Decide the hook for each one. The first line people hear. If you don't know the hook, you don't really know the reel yet.

4. Plan outfits and props in advance. Simple thing, but it stops every video from looking the same.

5. Shoot extra B-roll. Hands, products, the door opening, the space when it's busy. This fills the gaps when you edit.

So by the end of the day you have clips for the whole month, not just for this week.

The takeaway: the shoot is actually the easy part. The planning is what decides whether you post consistently or not.

This is how we plan content days for clients at Loyara.
